merger_description:
CRH Americas, Inc. (**CRH Americas**) proposes to indirectly acquire 100% of the shares in Arcosa, Ltd. (**Arcosa**) through its wholly owned subsidiary, Neon Merger Sub. Inc. (**Merger Sub**) (the **Acquisition**).

CRH Americas is a holding company owned by CRH plc (**CRH**, together with its direct and indirect subsidiaries, **CRH Group**), a global supplier of building materials and infrastructure products headquartered in Ireland and listed on the New York Stock Exchange (**NYSE**).

CRH has various interests in Australia, including controlling interests in CTC Precast Pty Ltd (**Civilmart**), Infrastructure Products Australia Pty Ltd (**IPA**) and Adbri Pty Ltd (**Adbri**). Each of Civilmart and IPA primarily supply precast concrete products that are used in a range of industries including infrastructure, telecommunications, water drainage, treatment and purification. Adbri is a national manufacturer and supplier of cement, ready-mix concrete and aggregate products.

Arcosa is headquartered in Dallas, Texas and is listed on the NYSE. Arcosa is a provider of infrastructure-related materials, products and solutions, predominantly in the United States, including:

* construction products, such as aggregates, specialty materials e.g. gypsum, hot-mix asphalt and construction site support; and
* engineered products, such as utility structures, poles, wind towers, telecom structures, traffic and lighting structures.

Arcosa has no subsidiaries, offices or employees, and supplies a very small volume of trenching and shoring products in Australia from its business in the US.

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap or vertical relationship
between CRH (including its connected entities) and Arcosa’s
activities in the supply of trenching and shoring products in
Australia
b. there are alternative suppliers of trenching and shoring
products in Australia
c. Arcosa has a small presence in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
